learning_outcomes.text: Learn the fundamental principles of electrical measurements, including obtaining voltages and currents using appropriate instruments and connections, as well as understanding and minimizing sources of error.
Discuss selected electrical measurement methods using signal generators and oscilloscopes.
Acquire the skills needed to create a report based on the measurements performed.
Obtain a basic idea about electronic measurements and about influences on these measurements.
Know how to use usual measurement devices and how they work.

syllabus_topics: Errors of the measurements (Absolute, Relative and Reduce Relative error, Class of precision)
Measurement of voltage divider (measurement of the voltage and current in voltage divider)
Measurement of input resistance (measurement of input resistance in dependence on the range)
Measurement of serial ADC (construction and calibration measurement of the serial ADC)
Measurement of parallel ADC (construction and calibration measurement of the parallel ADC)
Measurement with the oscilloscope (measurement by the raster, cursor and measure function, function trigger, transition processes)
Measurement of the resistivity (Ohm's law, bridges, Voltmeters method)
Measurement of the capacity (direct and indirect methods)
Measurement of the inductance (direct and indirect methods)
Measurement of frequency by Lissajous curve
Measurement of the frequency and phase shift by the using of the counter or oscilloscope
Measurement of the signal spectrum by the using of the FFT
Measurement of the AC voltmeter frequency dependence
assessment_rules: Credit conditions require the student to have measured all protocols and to have been absent less than three times. The examination consists of a consultation of the protocols where the student answers questions about the measurements. For distance learning, lessons are taught through MS Teams, which is equivalent to participation in lectures and exercises.
